items.title: Ray Vega interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 20, 2023
items.q: His name was Carl and we knew him. We knew him, he was a cop, he was a cop. He was a beat cop... this guy Carl lived in the projects and we all knew him

ctx.x: Dave Valentin, when I interviewed him, he said, this is a quote, he said, “My parents are from Puerto Rico, they migrated to New York and settled in the original South Bronx. It was a wonderful New York neighborhood, a mixed neighborhood, Italian, Jews, Greeks and Puerto Ricans, and a whole true community where there was really no problem getting along at all.” And he said, “I think they brought the old values into the community: be nice and do the right thing.”

Yeah. That’s how it was when I was growing up. And mind you we were in the Mott Haven which is one of the poorest parts of the poorest Congressional district in the United States. But when we were coming up the parents, the parents that moved their families into the projects, the projects were the next step up from living in the tenements. But one of our neighbors, which I didn’t find out until many, many years later, one of our neighbors was the Fleet family. And I always knew the Fleet family, you know they…
this guy Carl lived in the projects and we all knew him and the kids went to school in our neighborhood. It’s interesting.
